cases.prompt: On July 16, 2026, a six-person developer-tools startup has 42 paying teams and eight months of runway. The two founders still sell, support customers, review product decisions, and write code. Four engineers each own a product area and shipped the last six weekly releases on time. Customer response time is under four hours, no decision has waited more than one business day, and the team reports no recurring handoff failure. An investor says the company will look more mature for its next round if it hires a COO, appoints two engineering managers, and puts every engineer under a manager now. One founder likes the idea because her former employer used that structure; the other worries it will slow the team. Decide what organization changes, if any, the company should make over the next six weeks.
criteria: Selects `keep-flat` as the primary organization branch because no recurring coordination constraint is observed; rejects a COO, management layers, investor optics, title imitation, and large-company precedent as unsupported.

Classifies the six on-time releases, under-four-hour response time, under-one-business-day decision latency, direct product-area ownership, 42 paying teams, and eight months of runway as `observed`; classifies investor maturity advice, former-employer precedent, and both founders' interpretations as `claimed`; classifies founder-load sustainability, hidden rework, and the next actual coordination threshold as `unknown`; and gives each unknown an evidence owner, method or artifact, due date, threshold, and decision effect.

Preserves direct product-area ownership and the flat six-person shape; defines the smallest bounded monitoring or delegation test of founder load with named change and evidence owners, an artifact, baseline, six-week final review, continuity safeguard, and numeric or directly observable `keep-flat`, `change-process`, and `open-role` predicates.

States at least one recurring-coordination predicate from decision queues or cross-area failures and at least one leadership-capacity predicate from coaching span or founder work crowding out essential outcomes; before any search, requires a role charter with current outcomes, decision rights, hands-on work, interfaces, initial span, cost, 30/60/90-day evidence, and an expansion gate.

Returns a dated organization record with the current bottleneck decision, accountable owners, protected end-to-end ownership, six-week review, unresolved unknowns, and explicit keep-flat, change-process, and open-role branches.

cases.prompt: A 64-person B2B payments company has grown from 22 people in fourteen months. It now has product, engineering, sales, implementation, and support groups, but no written decision rights. The CEO, Ana, approves pricing exceptions, enterprise commitments, production incident priorities, senior hires, and every roadmap change. During the last eight weeks, 17 decisions waited at least five business days for Ana, three sales commitments reached engineering only after contracts were signed, and two customer incidents had duplicate responders but no single owner. Ana also still runs four weekly team meetings and says delegating means losing quality. Team leads disagree about who can say no to custom work. Customers are renewing and the company has fourteen months of runway. On July 16, 2026, design the next 45 days of organizational change without proposing a wholesale reorganization for its own sake.
criteria: Selects `decision-rights` as the primary branch for repeated queues and ambiguous authority; adds `leader-role-evolution` only for the separate Ana-centered mechanism with its own owner and test; preserves customer continuity; and rejects title-first or wholesale reorganization.

Diagnoses mechanisms from observed decision waits, late commitments, duplicate incident response, and overloaded founder approvals; separates Ana's quality concern and leads' interpretations as claims and marks the best durable decision boundaries, leadership capacity, and interface failure causes as unknown.

Defines a 45-day redesign with a named outcome owner for pricing, commitments, incidents, hiring, and roadmap changes; for each domain states decision limits, consultation or review, notification, escalation trigger, destination and deadline, backup, and audit artifact; uses a written decision-rights map and decision log; and reviews at days 15 and 45.

Retains Ana's preapproval only for predeclared irreversible, strategic, fiduciary, safety, legal, or exceptional-risk decisions; defines retained and delegated decisions, time allocation, product or customer contact, coaching, information flow, staged transfer, backup, succession, and rollback; preserves one end-to-end owner and clear customer-facing interfaces; and adds no unsupported reporting layer.

Returns a dated decision record with baseline measures, owners, 15- and 45-day reviews, and numeric or directly observable `keep`, `revise`, `add-capacity`, and `rollback-or-stop` thresholds tied to decision latency, unowned work, commitment quality, incidents, and founder load; `add-capacity` applies only if a sustained residual capacity gap remains after the decision and interface changes.

cases.prompt: A 14-person security startup has repeatable founder-led sales to 31 mid-market customers, but the founder can handle only six active opportunities at once and qualified deals now wait about 12 days for follow-up. The company wants its first sales leader. Candidate Elise was a regional VP at a large public company and presents a plan to hire eight representatives immediately. References confirm that she managed 45 people and consistently hit an established quota, but none saw her create a sales motion before product-market fit. Elise says her network will produce $4 million in pipeline in one quarter and asks for a cofounder title, executive decision rights, and an equity percentage before doing a work sample. The founders' own relationship and control are settled. The recruiting lead can run structured interviews, and two other candidates will complete work samples next week. Advise the company how to make the decision by August 7, 2026.
criteria: Selects `role-or-hire` as the primary branch for the employee sales-leader decision; makes no founder-status, control, or ownership decision inside hiring; if the company elects to consider Elise as a founder, hands that separate decision to `forming-founder-partnerships` before any status change; and does not reopen the settled relationship among the existing founders.

Separates observed deal load, follow-up delay, customer count, and reference-checked scale experience from Elise's claimed pipeline and treats early-motion building, startup fit, hands-on selling, hiring judgment, collaboration, and role evolution as unknown until tested.

Before selection, fixes the sales leader's current outcomes, decision domains, hands-on responsibilities, interfaces, and a concrete initial span, including zero direct reports if chosen; rejects the proposed eight-person hiring plan; and states an observable repeatability and residual-capacity predicate before any span expansion.

Uses the same job-relevant scorecard, structured questions, bounded accessible work sample, targeted references, evidence definitions, and critical threshold for every candidate; collects independent written ratings before discussion; selects exactly one of `hire`, `change-scope`, `continue-search`, or `no-hire`; and does not use pedigree, polish, confidence, or requested status as ability proxies.

Returns an August 7 hiring record with named evidence and decision owners, unresolved unknowns, compensation intent without inventing terms, and qualified current HR/counsel routing for employment, equity, background, and title details.

cases.prompt: On July 16, 2026, an 18-person hardware company has $900,000 in cash, fixed monthly obligations of $310,000, and dependable monthly gross profit of $55,000. A delayed certification means the next possible production revenue is five months away. Payroll is due in nine days, no signed financing exists, and the board asks the CEO for a plan tomorrow. Department ownership and reporting lines are clear, the team has no recurring coordination failures, and the founders' roles are settled. The CEO asks whether to add a chief of staff, reorganize into business units, and create a culture committee while also deciding what to do about cash. Advise the CEO on the primary decision and what organizational work belongs now.
criteria: Selects `route-away`; names `managing-runway-and-survival` as the exact canonical primary skill identifier because the company is default-dead on stated facts; and refuses to let organization design, a chief of staff, business units, or a culture committee displace the cash decision.

Uses the cash, obligations, gross profit, certification delay, payroll date, financing status, and settled organization as observed facts; treats future production revenue and unspecified financing as uncertain rather than rescue assumptions.

States that any irreversible employment, contractual, or legal consequence requires a current qualified HR or counsel owner; preserves certification and essential customer continuity; and requires a replacement protection before changing any material control.

Limits building-and-evolving-organizations to implementing role, ownership, communication, and workload consequences after the survival envelope and essential outcomes are chosen, with no unsupported layer or committee creation.

Returns a dated `route-away` handoff with the exact decision, exact composed skill identifiers in execution order, survival owner, next-day handoff, settled organization facts, later organization trigger, safeguards, preserved option, and switch condition; places `managing-runway-and-survival` before any later `building-and-evolving-organizations` work.

cases.prompt: A 36-person clinic-software company uses three cross-functional customer pods. Each pod nominally owns implementation through renewal, but the compensation plan pays sales entirely on signed annual value, implementation on on-time go-live, and support on tickets closed per day. In the last quarter, sales promised 11 unreviewed custom workflows, implementation marked seven clinics live with unresolved data issues, and support closed 19 tickets that reopened within a week. Renewal risk rose from 8% to 21%. Leaders now blame a weak culture and propose mandatory values training, a fourth approval committee, and individual rankings across every function. Interviews show pod members understand customer outcomes but say their incentives punish helping work outside their local metric. No evidence of fraud, harassment, retaliation, or a founder dispute has surfaced. Design an eight-week response.
criteria: Selects `incentive-or-culture` as the primary branch for the observed reward and ownership mechanism; adds `process-or-control` only for the separate pre-commitment mechanism with its own owner and test; and rejects values-slogan, individual-character, founder-partnership, and misconduct diagnoses unsupported by the evidence.

Separates observed promise, go-live, ticket, reopen, renewal-risk, and interview evidence from leaders' culture claim, and marks causal contribution, metric-gaming extent, workload capacity, and the best shared outcome measure as unknowns to test.

Preserves one accountable pod-level end-to-end customer outcome owner; defines a bounded eight-week prospective incentive and decision-rights test with change and evidence owners, start, two-week and eight-week reviews, artifacts, measures, and service-continuity, fairness, and legal safeguards; and adds no standing committee, reporting layer, or individual stack ranking.

Rejects the fourth committee and stack ranking; defines the smallest pre-commitment control for custom work, quality-complete go-live, and durable ticket closure; and names the harm prevented, accountable owner, response time, exception, escalation trigger, destination and deadline, audit artifact, direct and delay costs, expiry, and review.

Returns a dated organization record with baseline measures, compensation-change intent and current qualified HR or counsel review, and two- and eight-week reviews; sets numeric or directly observable `keep`, `revise`, `expand`, and `rollback-or-stop` thresholds tied to renewal risk, ticket reopen rate, unresolved-data go-lives, unreviewed custom promises, capacity overload, and recorded cross-functional ownership failures; and permits `expand` only when outcome, continuity, fairness, and harm thresholds pass, naming the next scope, owner, and review.
